xt:description.p: This plugin provides an AI-empowered markup assistant for editing TEI XML documents.

ul.li: Ref-to-Link works again: DILA's link service now expects the citation in the request body rather than the address, so <ref> to link had been failing for every reference with CBRD API error: HTTP 404. Traditional Chinese, full-width punctuation and quoted attributes pass through unchanged.

Ref-to-Link failures say what went wrong: "no matching reference" and "the service could not process this citation" are now distinct from "cannot reach the service", and the service's own explanation is shown. Previously every failure looked like a network error.
Protection against future service changes: The build checks the plugin's request format against DILA's published service description, so server-side changes surface before a release.

AI Markup now runs on the DILA server: The AI Markup action calls the DILA CBRD Parse endpoint (https://cbss.dila.edu.tw/cbrd/parse) instead of an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on your machine. The transformation model and its credentials stay on the server.

Preferences simplified: Six OpenAI-era fields are gone (parsing model, detection model, API key, base URL, chat path, AI timeout). Three replace them: CBRD Parse endpoint URL, CBRD Parse token, and CBRD Parse timeout (ms). Enter the shared DILA parse token once to resume work.

Clearer preference labels: The Ref-to-Link rows now read CBRD Link Endpoint and CBRD Link timeout (ms) so they are easy to tell apart from the CBRD Parse rows used by AI Markup, and the token row is renamed CBRD bearer token*: because that is what the service receives. The rows are ordered: CBRD Referer header, CBRD bearer token, CBRD Parse endpoint URL, CBRD Parse timeout (ms), CBRD Link Endpoint, CBRD Link timeout (ms), and every preference label reads the same in all three interface languages. Your saved settings are unchanged.

Rejected tokens are recognized correctly: A 401 "token rejected" response from the parse service is now reported as a credential problem instead of a connectivity error — even on Java 17, when the response has no readable body, and when Oxygen's own HTTP layer surfaces the 401 as HttpExceptionWithDetails ("401 Unauthorized for: <url>") instead of the JDK's usual exception — and the troubleshooting export records the cause.

Connectivity causes are exported: The troubleshooting export (schema 1.1.0) now includes a sanitized transportError field naming the exact exception (for example SocketTimeoutException: connect timed out) when a request never reached the service, so support no longer has to guess why a "cannot reach the service" message appeared.
No migration of old values: Any OpenAI settings left from a previous version are ignored, never reused, and never sent anywhere.

Document language is detected automatically: The request language comes from xml:lang on the document root element, so there is nothing to choose. Regional tags such as zh-Hant and ja-JP are understood; anything else defaults to Chinese.

Clearer failures: Each cause the DILA service reports now has its own actionable message, and "cannot reach the service", "no token configured", "token rejected", and "endpoint URL is wrong" are four distinct messages rather than one generic failure.
Checks before sending: An empty selection, a selection over 4,000 characters, a missing token, or a malformed endpoint URL are caught locally - no pointless round trip.
Timeout: Defaults to 30 seconds, matching the previous AI Markup timeout, because the server performs a model transformation.
Interrupted work is discarded: Closing the document or Oxygen mid-request cancels it; nothing is written into a closed document.

Unchanged: The review-then-replace workflow, undo history, editor responsiveness, diagnostics export, UTF-8 validation, and tag removal all behave as before. In Ref-to-Link only the request format changed; Replace, selection checks, retries and the configured endpoint are unchanged.
AI Markup Diagnostics: Added clearer cross-platform diagnostics for AI Markup request, credential, model, endpoint, and connectivity failures.
Sanitized Troubleshooting: Added sanitized diagnostic capture and export for support sharing.
Support Menu: Added User Manual and About to the gear menu, with installed-version and release-note visibility.
Error Display: Fixed error messages to show actual API error text instead of a generic invalid-response message.
API Endpoint Update: Updated CBRD API to the production endpoint.
Error Handling: Improved error message parsing for responses that provide a msg field.
Ref-to-Link Action: Convert selected <ref> elements to CBRD links and replace existing <ptr> safely.
CBRD Preferences: Configurable endpoint, referer, and timeout settings.
Validation and Errors: Clear feedback for invalid selections, missing components, and API failures.
Complete Java Migration: Migrated the implementation from JavaScript to pure Java for better performance and reliability.
Enhanced UTF-8 Tools: Improved file-encoding validation and conversion with automatic backup creation.
Oxygen integrated options/preferences page for setting the fine-tuned LLM models and API key.
Options saved with Oxygen's wsOptionsStorage approach.
API key saved and retrieved with better security by Oxygen's secretOption.
Fixed an API-key handling issue that caused an error after saving options.
Added multi-language support for the plugin.
Added a custom options/preferences page for LLM models and API key configuration.
Initial AI-driven markup for unmarked references.
Initial TEI tag-removal support.
